name: referent-retrieval/codec-invariances
says: For each material a referent can be mentioned in: how a region is addressed, what its codec decodes it into, what the codec treats as accidental (not followed), what it drops, how each bound is to be measured, what evidence the material supplies, and how it can be forged. A bound is never a number typed here: it is a recipe and a state, and an unmeasured bound means equality is exact-hash only. Companion to the janus Ground@1 drafts (statement-equivalence strict and casual), whose `dependency` event is the text invariance below.

events.material: text (a language; the source here is English Wikipedia wikitext reduced to prose)
events.by: Claude (Sonnet 5.5), a draft for the project owner to ratify or replace
events.says: A region is a byte span of the decoded plain text, with the sha256 of exactly those bytes and of the whole text. The decode into EOT is khora's reader for the declared language (readDocument, the one door), never a code default; the language is read from the source's declared language and recorded on the entry. Letter case, spacing and compatibility forms of a character (a ligature, a full-width digit) are accidental and are not followed. Every other token is followed, marks included: a currency sign, a minus sign, a negation. A stated time or tense is a statement like any other. What the wikitext-to-prose step drops is part of this codec's disclosed loss and is counted, never hidden.

address.hash: sha256 of the span bytes and of the whole text

decode.piece: khora native/reading.js readDocument (priors from janus; lexicon off unless the hyperlexicon door answers)
decode.language: declared by the source, recorded on the entry, AND heard by khora's language context; a read whose declared and heard languages disagree is refused (E3: a French sentence read as eng returns no gap, so the reader will not catch it)
decode.claims: kernel/gfp-claim.js (ground, roles ARG0/ARG1, relation, polarity, force)
decode.time: kernel/temporal-reference.js, narrative-time.js (tense as anaphora; a time is a referent)

accidental.case: accidental for NOMINATING only; kept when deciding that two names are the same name (row 35 E1: folding adds 235 hits at 0.396 gold)
accidental.note: case is accidental for tokens (janus dependency event) but janus's identity event keeps letter case for names in both the strict and the casual ground: an unresolved tension, see owner-decisions[0]

followed: numerals with their sign and unit; a scale written as a word is NOT compared by the number parser and is left to a declared reader

loss.source-reduction: wikitext to prose drops: templates, tables, reference tags, files and categories, headings, and every line starting with a list, indent or table mark; links inside dropped material are lost
loss.counted: links in prose and links dropped as unplaceable are reported with every run (row 30: 9,228 and 0)
loss.reader: only names are reliably referents; noun-phrase referents come from the opt-in descriptor lane, not run by us; 10% of clauses hold two named referents (row 29)

source-reduction-measured.note: DEV, 30 articles; captions are the material of the image-caption codec, templates are structured data (scorer only), citations are their own material

evidence: claims with polarity, role, ground and time

forgeable.surface-facts: an informed impostor writes the same facts and is judged equivalent (rows 26-27); a verdict resting only on them carries that rate and caps at Hold

body.falsifier: a pair equal within the declared invariances whose decodes differ in a claim that matters to the asker; or a wikitext-to-prose drop that removes a claim the asker's concern needs and is not counted

events.by: Claude (Sonnet 5.5), a draft for the project owner to ratify or replace
events.says: A region is a box in an image with the sha256 of the DECODED PIXELS inside the box (not of the file), and of the whole decoded image. The decode into EOT carries only what a named provider reads out of the region as a claim: text inside the box (OCR), a class label with its provider named, a caption, alt text and provenance with its basis. Look itself is not a claim: a nearest neighbour in an embedding is a nominator and never decodes into EOT. Until each accidental transform has a measured bound, equality of two regions is exact pixel hash only; a resized, recompressed or cropped copy is a NOMINATION, never an equal.

address.hash: PINNED DECODE: sha256 of the file, decoder name, version and settings, the box, and sha256 of the decoded pixels in the box
address.reopen: re-decodes with the pinned decoder and refuses if the pin or either hash differs; lossless formats preferred (row 35 E4: one JPEG gave 5 distinct decoded-pixel hashes across decoders, one PNG gave 1)
address.duplicates: exact duplicates by hash, never by embedding

pieces: Slate sidecars: tesseract on-screen text, Apple Vision classes and faces, keyframes
decode.claims: text-in-region, provider-named class labels with confidence, caption, alt text, provenance with basis
decode.nominator: an image embedder (none installed; a download needs the owner's explicit yes naming file, source and size)

accidental-classes: a crop that keeps the whole region of interest
followed: text and numbers inside the region (OCR)
orientation and mirroring (a flip changes text)
counts and positions of marked items
any difference an asker's concern depends on

bounds.state: UNMEASURED: bound_unmeasured for every accidental class
bounds.recipe: per transform class, the largest change at which a region's nearest-neighbour agreement with its original stays above the agreement of that region with random other regions (a seeded null built the house way: the same population, leave-one-out, max over seeded draws, intersection of two seeds with the dissent kept)
bounds.until-then: equality is exact pixel hash only

loss.not-run: a provider that did not run is reported not run, never zero (Slate: faces null)
loss.text: OCR text only where tesseract ran; small or stylised text may be missed
loss.look: appearance beyond the provider's labels is not in the reading

evidence: source and provenance (a basis such as 'inferred from filename' is a lead, not a record)

forgeable.look: a look-alike logo or a re-cut image passes a similarity; an informed impostor can pass any single visual channel
forgeable.cap: Hold with a hunger list: caption, OCR text, source

body.people: no similarity search over face regions to identify a natural person; a verdict needs a text tie. OWNER TO CONFIRM (my reading, not legal advice)
body.falsifier: a region declared equal within an accidental class whose OCR text or labelled claims differ in a way that matters; or an image-only verdict above Hold that an informed look-alike passes

events.material: audio, and the audio track of video
events.by: Claude (Sonnet 5.5), a draft for the project owner to ratify or replace
events.says: A region is a time range with the sha256 of the DECODED samples in the range at a declared sample rate and channel layout, and of the whole decoded stream. The decode into EOT carries only what a named provider reads out as a claim: a transcript segment (machine-made; segments over music or noise are moved to suppressed, never deleted), a sound class with its provider named, a tempo or key only where it beats a shuffled null (otherwise 'not above chance', unpitched or ambiguous), on-screen text for the picture, and provenance with its basis. A cut or an address boundary lands only on a real silence; a boundary that cannot be snapped is not safe. Until each accidental transform has a measured bound, equality of two ranges is exact sample hash only.

address.hash: sha256 of the decoded samples in the range and of the whole stream
address.reopen: re-decodes and refuses if either hash differs
address.boundaries: snapped to silence (slate snap); snapped:false means do not cut

pieces: Slate sidecars: whisper.cpp transcript, SoundAnalysis classes, keyframes, on-screen text, tempo and key against a shuffled null
decode.claims: transcript segment, class label with provider, tempo or key with its chance level, provenance with basis

followed: the words said (confirm any quote or number with slate window before use)
who is speaking where the speaker is attested
tempo and key only where above chance
any difference an asker's concern depends on

bounds.state: UNMEASURED: bound_unmeasured for every accidental class; the time tolerance of a range address is an OWNER DECISION
bounds.recipe: per transform class, the largest change at which a transcript's word timings and a range's neighbour agreement stay above their seeded nulls, measured leave-one-out; recogniser word times drift, so a range edge is never trusted without a snap
bounds.until-then: equality is exact sample hash only

loss.suppressed: segments over music or noise are suppressed, not deleted
loss.not-run: a provider that did not run is reported not run, never zero
loss.heuristic: sound labels from the heuristic provider (modulated, sustained, silence) are relative to the file and do not name sounds
loss.sync: a lip-sync lag is a lead to confirm, never a verdict (the pre-registered validation missed its bars)
loss.non-speech: base.en invented 1 word over 5 non-speech controls (digital silence); a segment with no speech evidence is suppressed, not trusted
loss.numerals: the decode writes spoken numbers as digits ('nineteen twelve' -> 1912): numerals need their own codec step

evidence: on-screen text over the same range

forgeable.audio: a re-cut or re-recorded range passes a similarity; a voice or a mouth rhythm is not an identity
forgeable.cap: Hold with a hunger list: transcript, on-screen text, provenance

body.falsifier: a range declared equal within an accidental class whose transcript or class claims differ in a way that matters; or a cut accepted at an unsnapped point

accidental-attested-at-claim-level.state: LEAD (one synthesised utterance, one voice, whisper base.en, one run each; row 35 E5)
accidental-attested-at-claim-level.note: decoded samples differ in every case, so region equality stays exact-sample-hash while the transcript claim is invariant

owner-decisions: text: the janus drafts (strict AND casual) disagree with themselves on case: the dependency event says letter case is accidental and not followed, the identity event says a name is the same name when spelled the same with letter case KEPT. Which holds for names in referent retrieval (case kept, or folded under the codec's accidental set)?
text: is the wikitext-to-prose reduction an accepted decode for Wikipedia sources, with dropped links counted on every run?
text: the language of each read is declared by the source and recorded; confirm that code defaults such as language eng are to be removed from the experiment scripts
image: accept exact decoded-pixel hash as the only equality until the bounds are measured?

image: confirm the people policy (nominate-only, a text tie required, no identification of private individuals)

who bylines and adopts each codec (adoptedBy is null until a named reader adopts it)
